meta.about_video_description: Luther Aloud is a YouTube channel that narrates Martin Luther's works — one work per episode, in the order he wrote them, from the Ninety-Five Theses of 1517 through the sermons, commentaries, and letters of his last years. The video is a still cover with the narration playing over it; the audio is the point, the picture is a frame.
meta.totals_note: The Holman treatises, the Lenker sermons and commentaries, and the standalone classics — treated as one corpus, in the order they were written.

phases.source: The Standard Edition of Luther's Works, ed. John Nicholas Lenker (1903–1909). Digitized on the Internet Archive; index links via Reformed Books Online.
phases.note: Sermon collections are one episode per sermon — the natural unit — so the episode count grows large. The groupings follow the Lenker Edition's own volume order, which runs through the church year (Advent, Epiphany, Easter, Trinity) rather than by composition date. Individual titles are TBD.
